# OKX Hackathon Community Guide — Agent Context

Last source review: 2026-10-17. This is an independent community guide, not an official OKX publication. The official links below are authoritative when product behavior or commands change.

## Product boundaries

OKX TR Agent Trade Kit (ATK) connects OKX exchange capabilities to a local MCP server and CLI. Agent Skills teach coding agents how to invoke the CLI. OnchainOS is a separate onchain developer stack. OKX.ai is a separate agent marketplace built on OnchainOS capabilities. Do not describe the latter two as ATK modules.

## ATK: read-only first

Official sources: https://github.com/okx/agent-trade-kit and https://tr.okx.com/docs-v5/agent_en/#introduction

ATK market data includes ticker, order book, candles, recent trades, and some derivatives metrics. The installed package version determines the exact available tools. Do not rely on a hard-coded total tool count: official pages can lag behind the repository.

Prerequisite: Node.js 18 or newer, according to the ATK repository.

Install:

```bash
npm install -g @okx_ai/okx-trade-mcp @okx_ai/okx-trade-cli
```

Use the TR site explicitly: the CLI and MCP otherwise default to global. `OKX_SITE=tr` was verified against a public BTC-USDT ticker request. First public query, no API key required:

```bash
OKX_SITE=tr okx market ticker BTC-USDT
```

Start a local MCP server with public market data only:

```bash
okx-trade-mcp --site tr --modules market
```

Codex CLI registration:

```bash
codex mcp add okx-tr-market -- okx-trade-mcp --site tr --modules market
codex mcp list
```

Detailed Codex setup: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/atk/setup-codex

Claude Code direct registration:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio okx-tr-market -- okx-trade-mcp --site tr --modules market
```

Detailed Claude Code setup: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/atk/setup-claude-code

Cursor MCP configuration (merge this server into any existing mcpServers object):

```json
{"mcpServers":{"okx-tr-market":{"command":"okx-trade-mcp","args":["--site","tr","--modules","market"]}}}
```

Detailed Cursor setup: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/atk/setup-cursor

The 1.4.8 ATK `setup` helper does not accept a `--site` flag. Direct registration is needed to select the TR endpoint explicitly.

Source for ATK setup and flags: https://github.com/okx/agent-trade-kit/blob/github-main/docs/configuration.md
Source for Codex MCP command shape: https://developers.openai.com/learn/docs-mcp

ATK CLI examples:

```bash
OKX_SITE=tr okx market ticker BTC-USDT
OKX_SITE=tr okx market candles BTC-USDT --bar 1H --limit 10
OKX_SITE=tr okx market funding-rate BTC-USDT-SWAP
```

CLI subcommands are separated by spaces. MCP tool identifiers use another naming form; do not invent CLI commands by transforming MCP names. Current CLI reference: https://github.com/okx/agent-trade-kit/blob/github-main/docs/cli-reference.md

Install only the public market-data Agent Skill in the coding agent's project directory (replace the agent ID with `claude-code` or `cursor` as appropriate):

```bash
npx --yes skills add okx/agent-skills --skill okx-cex-market --agent codex --copy --yes
```

The skill requires the `okx` CLI. `--skill` avoids installing account/trading skills in a read-only starter. The command was verified in a temporary project for Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor. Official skill list: https://github.com/okx/agent-skills ; installer options: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills

## Market Risk Copilot example

Request BTC-USDT ticker, first five order-book levels, and the last six completed 1-hour candles. Calculate midpoint = (best_bid + best_ask) / 2, spread_bps = (best_ask - best_bid) / midpoint * 10000, and the range from the lowest low to highest high of completed candles. Include instrument, source tools, and timestamps. Never fabricate missing values. The site's interactive example uses simulated numbers; it is not a live feed.

## Safety

Public market data needs no API key. Account queries require authorized read access. Trading and account changes require suitable permissions and product availability. Keep credentials in local configuration, never in chat, source control, a browser page, or a public demo. Default to read-only modules. Before any real order, transfer, withdrawal, wallet signature, or account-setting change, show parameters and impact and obtain explicit human confirmation. Demo mode is for simulation, but not every product or endpoint is available there. Regional and account restrictions still apply. Official safety source: https://tr.okx.com/docs-v5/agent_en/#safety

## OnchainOS

Official overview: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/home/what-is-onchainos
Official agent wallet quickstart: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/home/install-your-agentic-wallet

OnchainOS covers Agentic Wallet, onchain market data, DEX trading, and agent payments. The documented installer is:

```bash
npx -y @okxweb3/onchainos-installer install
```

Begin with a read-only market lookup. Wallet creation, transaction signatures, swaps, and payments are separate actions requiring their own review and appropriate user approval. Never request seed phrases or private keys in chat.

## OKX.ai

Official overview: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/okxai/what-is-okxai
User registration guide: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/okxai/user-register
ASP overview: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/okxai/asp

OKX.ai is an agent marketplace with User, Agent Service Provider (ASP), and Evaluator roles. ASPs can provide repeatable A2MCP services or negotiated A2A tasks. Registration, paid tasks, escrow, evaluation, and staking are real external actions. The community guide explains their flow but does not perform them.

## Suggested starter task

"Use OKX TR Agent Trade Kit's public market tools to inspect BTC-USDT. Retrieve ticker, the first five order-book levels, and the last six completed 1-hour candles. Calculate bid/ask spread in basis points and the completed-candle price range. Cite the tools and data timestamps. Do not place orders, access my account, invent missing data, or ask for credentials."

## Hackathon project ideas

### Avalanche Builder Hub and judging preparation

Team1 referral for Avalanche Builder Hub account creation: https://go.team1.network/turkiye-builder . The link redirects to Builder Hub with a referral parameter. A Builder Hub account is not hackathon registration, admission, project submission, or proof of an onchain deployment. Official account guide: https://build.avax.network/academy/avalanche-l1/avalanche-fundamentals/04-creating-an-l1/01a-create-builder-account . Official Fuji C-Chain deployment guide: https://build.avax.network/blog/deploy-a-dapp-on-c-chain-with-foundry . Official ICM overview: https://build.avax.network/docs/cross-chain/avalanche-warp-messaging/overview . Checked 2026-10-17.

The user supplied a **suggested judging workbook**, not verified official event rules. Its draft weights are: Agentic Design 20% (end-to-end autonomy; reasoning and appropriate tool use); Technical Execution 15% (working deployed product; architecture; technical difficulty); Avalanche Integration 10% (real C-Chain or Avalanche L1 deployment; meaningful use of Avalanche strengths); OKX Integration 10% (actual OKX tooling; plausible OKX.ai service path); Innovation & Real-World Value 25% (originality, clear user problem, market or business model, go-to-market readiness); Demo & Presentation 20% (working live demo, UX, pitch and Q&A). The workbook proposes a preliminary eligibility check for a public repository, working demo, Avalanche deployment, and at least one OKX tool, plus Agentic Design as a tie-breaker. Do not present these as confirmed event requirements. Its instruction to average four subcriteria is inconsistent with rows containing two or three; do not invent a numerical scoring formula.

For every project, prepare evidence: a runnable public repo; a short agent trace showing goal, multi-step plan, tool calls, results, failure handling, and human approval gates; a dated real OKX tool response; a live demo with a clearly labeled fallback recording; a target user and value proposition. Claim Avalanche integration only when a component is genuinely deployed on C-Chain/Fuji or an Avalanche L1 and provide the chain, contract address, and explorer or transaction link. A Vercel deployment and Builder Hub registration are not onchain deployment. Keep future OKX.ai service plans distinct from current integration. Turkish Avalanche guide: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/avalanche/intro . Judging checklist in Start: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/start/judging .

Use https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/start/intro to select a path by goal and client. Three runnable recipes are available: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/build/atk-data-quality (public read-only ATK data, local fixture first), https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/build/atk-a2mcp (local JSON HTTP service, not MCP or A2MCP registration), and https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/build/payment-402 (local simulated HTTP 402, no real payment). Corresponding project prompts: https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/ai/prompts/atk-data-quality.txt , https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/ai/prompts/atk-a2mcp.txt , and https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/ai/prompts/payment-402.txt . The local payment demo's `x-demo-approved` header is a fake switch, never payment proof.

The Turkish idea hub at https://agentic-hackathon-tr.vercel.app/guide/ideas/intro proposes 40 mostly non-trading weekend MVPs: 21 ATK ideas, 11 OnchainOS payment and wallet-experience ideas, and 8 OKX.ai agent-service ideas. The ATK section groups ideas by feasibility: public market data (no key), news tools (verify installed version and regional access), private account data (Read-authorized API access; use fixtures first), local audit logs (verify installed version), and a cross-product data-service example. New public-market ideas cover closed-candle education, data availability, order-book depth visualization, agent query budgeting, and fact checking against timestamped responses. The new OnchainOS ideas cover simulated payment-record privacy and paid API recovery; new OKX.ai ideas cover simulated A2A task recovery and blinded service evaluation. These workflows are project designs, not built-in OKX tools. Highlighted starts are an ATK data-quality dashboard, an ATK-based agent service with simulated payment, and an HTTP 402 payment-flow simulator. These are community proposals, not shipped OKX products, official contest categories, guaranteed winners, or proof that live APIs are available without developer access. ATK itself does not provide OnchainOS payments or the OKX.ai marketplace; cross-product ideas require separate integration. Distinguish HTTP Seller from Agent Seller payment support, including methods currently marked coming soon in the official API overview: https://web3.okx.com/onchainos/dev-docs/payments/api-overview . For every mock, label simulated data and show costs, permissions, state, assumptions, and missing evidence. Keep real orders, swaps, wallet signatures, transfers, payments, subscriptions, marketplace registration, and staking outside starter demos.
